title: North Lake Marketplace adaptive capacity & cost matrix - POC bench notes
content:
Summary:
This document captures benchmarking notes from the North Lake Marketplace POC run (pilot customer: North Lake, mid-market ecommerce). The goal was to evaluate cost/perf tradeoffs for search-ranking and short-form generation endpoints under a realistic mixed workload, and to produce an adaptive capacity/cost matrix that the Solutions team can hand to the customer for sizing and pricing conversations.

POC objectives:
- Validate per-route SLOs: median < 40ms for ranking calls (seq=64), median < 120ms for short-generation (seq=256).
- Determine cost per 1M tokens for the two primary routes at 95th-percentile concurrency targets (50 and 200 concurrent users respectively).
- Characterize warm-cache vs cold-cache behavior and quantify headroom required for 99th percentile latency.
- Evaluate heterogeneous placement: mix of H100 for low-latency routes and L4 for cheaper throughput.

Test environment:
- Redwood runtime: release v1.18.4 (kernel selector enabled).
- Models: rdlw-v2-rank-7B (FP16), rdlw-v3-chat-13B (q4_0 quantized).
- Hardware: H100 (2x48GB), A100-40GB, L4-48GB. We provisioned: 4xH100 nodes, 3xA100 nodes, 6xL4 nodes behind the dedicated pool.
- Network: eu-west-1 region (customer wanted EU placement).
- Client harness: k6 + custom tokenized workload generator to simulate bursty QPS with diurnal pattern.

Workload profiles:
- Ranking route (search-rank): 64 token average, 80ms think-time, steady 50 QPS target ramped to 200 QPS for burst window. Typical input batchable; request pattern is highly parallel across sessions.
- Generation route (summary-gen): average 256 tokens, streaming enabled, typical per-user QPS low but variable; concurrency target 200 active sessions for peak traffic.
- Mixed traffic scenario: 70% search-rank, 30% summary-gen by QPS; spike test: 3x baseline for 90s to emulate campaign.

Methodology:
- For each placement (H100-only, H100+L4 hybrid, L4-only for gen), we measured: median, p95, p99 latencies for both routes; token/sec throughput; GPU utilization; CPU and network overhead; and per-token cost estimate using current dedicated pricing model.
- Cold-cache run: nodes restarted and warmed over 30 minutes, then burst test applied to capture cold-path penalties (KV cache miss + model cache population).
- Batching sweeps: batch sizes 1, 4, 8, 16 applied to ranking route to find latency vs efficiency sweet spot under latency SLOs.

Key results (aggregated):
- H100-only placement:
  - search-rank: median=22ms, p95=68ms, p99=125ms at 200 QPS with batch size=4. GPU utilization 72-85%. Cost: estimated $38 per 1M tokens (ranking tokens counted as tokens in/out).
  - summary-gen: median=95ms (streaming first-chunk), p95=280ms, p99=520ms at 200 concurrent sessions. Throughput: ~420 tokens/sec per H100. Cost: $92 per 1M tokens.
- H100+L4 hybrid (rank on H100, gen on L4 with autoscaling):
  - search-rank: median=25ms, p95=82ms, p99=150ms. Slightly higher p99 due to cross-pool network hop when fallback triggered. Cost for rank route: $29 per 1M tokens (savings from moving other load off H100).
  - summary-gen on L4 (q4_0): median=130ms first-chunk, p95=380ms, p99=760ms. Throughput per L4: 220 tokens/sec. Cost: $48 per 1M tokens.
  - Observed benefit: total platform cost reduced ~28% for combined workload vs H100-only, but summary p99 increased.
- L4-only (baseline low-cost configuration):
  - search-rank: median=58ms, p95=190ms, p99=420ms at same QPS; batch size=8 needed to keep throughput acceptable. Cost: $16 per 1M tokens but fails the median SLO for ranking.

Cold vs warm behavior:
- Cold-cache effect noticeable on ranking route: initial 90s window after deploy showed p95 spike to 280ms and p99 > 1.2s due to KV-cache and model weight paging. Warmed state returned to baseline after ~120s of sustained traffic.
- Recommendation: pre-warm strategy (rolling canary + synthetic warm traffic) reduces cold-window p99 by ~65% in our runs.

Batching tradeoffs (ranking route):
- Batch 1: median 18ms, high GPU inefficiency (util 45%); cost high per token.
- Batch 4: median 22ms, util 75% — best tradeoff meeting median SLO and reduced unit cost.
- Batch 8: median 36ms, improves cost slightly but starts to breach p95 SLO occasionally during bursts.

Observations and subtle effects:
- Response variance: summary-gen p99 is dominated by tail tokens (finalization + streaming flush). Enabling chunked streaming with aggressive flush thresholds shaved ~60ms off p99 in experiments.
- Heterogeneous placement introduced occasional cross-pool fallbacks that increased p99 for rank route; routing policy needs stricter affinity (pin rank to H100 unless overloaded).
- Quantization (q4_0) on the 13B chat variant reduced memory pressure and enabled more concurrency per L4, but introduced small degradation in generation quality detectable in internal BLEU-ish heuristics. Customer accepted q4_0 for non-customer-facing drafts; recommended mixed strategy with full-precision for high-value endpoints.

Action items and recommendations for the customer:
1) Baseline proposal: hybrid placement (rank on H100 pool, gen on autoscaling L4 pool) with batch size 4 for rank, streaming with chunk size 64 for gen. This meets median SLOs and reduces expected monthly unit cost ~28% vs H100-only.
2) Sizing table (per 1M QPS tokens monthly): provide 3 tiers — PPS (pilot) / Business / Peak — with node counts and estimated cost. (See attached spreadsheet reference in Confluence).
3) Pre-warm runbook: add warm traffic step in deploy pipeline; include thresholds to keep a rolling warm window for each model variant.
4) Rollout plan: start with conservative affinity routing and monitor p99; enable progressive relaxation of affinity if sustained headroom observed.
5) Eval gating: add prompt-set-based quality regression checks when enabling q4_0 for gen route.

Appendix (sample raw measurements):
- Ranking route at 200 QPS, H100-only, batch=4: median 22ms, mean 28ms, p90 54ms, p95 68ms, p99 125ms, GPU util 78%, tokens/sec per node 11.2k.
- Generation route at 200 concurrent, hybrid L4 pool size 6: median 130ms, p95 380ms, p99 760ms, tokens/sec aggregate 1.35k across L4 pool.
- Cost calc notes: used dedicated per-hour rates from pricing table (H100 $8.4/hr equivalent in pool config, L4 $1.9/hr) plus overhead for networking and platform fees (applied 12% uplift). Token accounting includes both prompt and response tokens; streaming per-chunk overhead counted as +2 tokens per chunk.

Notes to SE team:
- Need follow-up run with the customer's real prompt set to validate quantization quality assumptions.
- Test add-on: evaluate 8-bit quantization path (q8_0) which may further reduce gen cost while preserving quality for targeted prompts.
- Log correlation: record model hash + kernel selection to trace occasional 200-400ms outliers observed in H100-only runs.

Concluding statement:
The North Lake POC shows a clear cost/latency frontier where hybrid placement reaches a favorable point for the customer: acceptable medians for both routes while reducing unit cost materially. The main risks are cold-start behavior and gen-route p99 under quantization — both addressable with pre-warm and a cautious rollout strategy.

Prepared by: Ethan Cho
QA notes: reviewed with Priya N., Marcus L., and Sofia A. on 2028-06-20.
